To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pyrolyzed products from the waste biomass examined can be used in energetic and agricultural applications.

(1) The pyrolysis gases from the agricultural waste materials examined were suitable for energy production; (2) The biochars produced could be used as soil amendments and as liming agents; (3) The alkaline metals were leached in large amounts, but the heavy metals were not.
the biochars produced from agricultural wastes from the olive oil industry, when mixed with swine sludge, could be used as soil amendment and liming agents, providing plant nutrients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the valorization of waste materials for energy and environmental purposes.
the development of new technologies for energy recovery from agricultural waste materials, as well as for their valorization as soil amendment.

the evaluation of the energetic and environmental potential of waste biomass, in order to provide an alternative solution for the management of these wastes and to contribute to the development of a sustainable society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the waste materials examined in the present study could be considered as a valuable resource for energetic and environmental purposes.
the biochars produced from the pyrolysates of the agricultural wastes from the petrochemical industry are suitable for soil amendment, while those of the sludge are more appropriate for liming.
the pyrolytic products from the blends of industrial swine sludges and oil wastes can be used as a source of energy and for soil amendment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pyrolysis is a suitable process for the valorization of waste materials for energy production and soil amendment.
the biochar produced from the pyroysis of the waste biomass blends can be used as liminig agent or for soil amendment, providing plant nutrients.
the pyrolytic conversion of waste materials can be considered an environmentally friendly and economically sustainable technology for the production of biofuels and biochars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pyrolysis could be used to convert industrial waste materials into useful products.
the pyrolytic conversion of the wastes examined is a promising way to valorize the wastes for energy and agronomy.

the biochars from the blends of swine sludge with agricultural wastes from oil industry can be used as limings or as a soil amendment providing plant nutrient, and their use can reduce the amount of waste disposed in landfills.
